title: Elastic IO Floor and Per-Token Split Pricing Experiment for Hosted API
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Run a controlled experiment to test an elastic minimum (floor) that adjusts based on per-customer IO distribution and SLA tiering, paired with differentiated input/output per-token rates for streaming and non-streaming requests. The goal is to reduce billing friction for low-IO interactive apps while protecting unit economics for long-context or high-output workloads. The experiment surface should include: (1) an algorithmic floor that decays to zero below a usage volatility threshold, (2) separate input/output token price multipliers for streaming vs. non-streaming, and (3) an enterprise override path for committed minimums with contract-discount bindings.
background: Multiple prior probes surfaced two competing pressures: product teams want simpler meters for developers (single per-token price) while finance and sales want protections against pathological usage patterns (very large model outputs generating excess cost). Prior experiments focused on anchored ladders and asymmetric IO splits, but we lack a live test of an dynamic floor tied to traffic shape and SLO tier. Sales has an increasing number of asks for explicit minimums in security questionnaires; legal asks for clear language in contracts about how streaming differs from non-streaming billing. This experiment aims to give sales tools and engineering confidence in predictable economics.
proposed_experiment:
1) Enroll a 10% randomized cohort of new hosted API customers and a 5% cohort of enterprise trial customers.
2) Compute per-customer 28-day IO distribution (median output token ratio, 95th pct output bursts).
3) Apply an elastic floor: customers with low volatility and median output < 2x input get floor=0; customers above thresholds get floor = min( base_floor * volatility_factor, capped_floor ). Base_floor starts at $5/month equivalent.
4) Apply per-token multipliers: streaming_output_multiplier = 1.15, non_streaming_output_multiplier = 1.00; input tokens get a discounted multiplier = 0.6 to encourage richer prompts.
5) Offer enterprise commit override: sales can lock in a flat minimum in exchange for % discount and SLAs.
6) Duration: 8 weeks with mid-experiment telemetry review at week 3.
7) Controls: identical cohort with current baseline pricing to measure delta in ARPC and churn.
8) Billing UX: prime the invoice line items with "elastic floor adjustment" and provide dashboard transparency for customers enrolled.

Note: the exact multiplier values are initial hypotheses and will be tuned after the statistical pre-check (see analysis_plan).
success_metrics: Primary: net revenue per customer cohort (ARPC) delta vs control; Secondary: churn at 30/60 days, # of disputed invoices, average cost-per-token to Redwood, percent of cohort hitting floor, sales enablement conversions (signed deals referencing commit override). Experiment will be considered for rollout if ARPC delta >= +3% with no increase in disputes and churn <= baseline + 0.5ppt.
analysis_plan: Pre-experiment checks: distributional balance test between treatment & control on historical IO ratio and ARR. Statistical plan: difference-in-differences on ARPC, bootstrap confidence intervals for churn and disputes, stop-loss rule if disputes exceed 2% of invoices in week 1-2. Attribution: tag usage by request type (streaming true/false), model family, and customer tier. Run cost-model simulation daily to monitor unit economics; trigger rollback in case marginal cost delta > 8% and revenue delta < 1%.
rollout_plan: Week 0: feature flags and billing pipeline changes in staging; Week 1: small pilot (2% of new signups) for smoke tests; Week 2-3: ramp to target cohorts and begin telemetry collection; Week 6: mid-experiment review with Sales/Finance/Legal to review contract impacts and security questionnaire language; Week 8: final analysis and product decision (promote to 'billing-2026-q2' or iterate). If promoted, default to 25% of new customers and gated enterprise opt-in for committed minimums until next quarter's evaluation.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customer confusion leading to increased billing disputes. Mitigation: explicit invoice line items and email drip explaining enrollment. Risk: adverse unit economics from high-output streaming models. Mitigation: conservative streaming_output_multiplier and stop-loss rule; monitor model-level cost and block if needed. Risk: Sales/Legal contract complexity. Mitigation: create templated language for commit overrides and surface clear examples in the security questionnaire pack. Risk: Implementation latency in billing system. Mitigation: isolate experiment via feature-flagged billing router and shadow billing runs before charging.
security_questionnaire_items: Does the vendor enforce minimum billing amounts for API usage? - Answer: dynamic floors with customer-visible thresholds and enterprise commit options.
How are streaming and batch API calls billed differently? - Answer: streaming output tokens are billed under a separate multiplier; invoices break out streaming vs non-streaming line items.
Are customer-specific minimums auditable? - Answer: yes, dashboard shows enrollment, floor calculations, and historical invoice adjustments.
